classification_rule: A failure is a harness defect when the recorded observation contradicts the harness code rather than the product contract; the runtime stays the candidate under test and only tests/pp4-core-campaign/** may change.

attempts.outcome: FAILED at phase 7 (host reboot and identity recovery)
attempts.observed: jq: error: Could not open file /home/tester/pp4-evidence/durable-bootstrap-after-reboot.json: No such file or directory
attempts.root_cause: in-vm-core-post.sh dumped the durable-state snapshot with json.dump(..., sys.stdout) but without the `>"$EVID/..."` redirection that in-vm-core-acceptance.sh uses, so the evidence file was never created; set -o pipefail then turned the following jq read into an abort
product_evidence_from_this_attempt: phases 0-6 PASS including the bounded Horizon witness (login, project context, identity/images/networks/instances panels, pagination guard, compute API selector, native resource visible)
Horizon independence PASS and Horizon restart recovery PASS

attempts.classification: operator abort, not a product or campaign failure
attempts.reason: the manifest replay-gate definition still had to be corrected and the final harness must be identical for Ubuntu and Debian, so the run was stopped before the post-reboot reinstall phases

attempts.outcome: FAILED at phase 8 (exact public installer rerun)
attempts.root_cause: the TLS identity gate hashed /etc/o3k/tls/* as the unprivileged campaign user, but the agent and server private keys are root-only; sha256sum exited 1 and set -o pipefail aborted the campaign
product_evidence_from_this_attempt: phases 0-7 PASS including the bounded Horizon witness, Horizon independence, Horizon restart and post-reboot identity/durable-state observation
phase-7 durable snapshot (written by the fixed step) shows the BuildingBlock ready and the Placement provider Enabled

attempts.outcome: FAILED on SSH transport during the reboot boundary
attempts.classification: harness defect (reboot gate was vacuous and racy)
observed: Connection to 127.0.0.1 closed by remote host.
core acceptance log unavailable (scp status=255, status=255)
the retained guest was up with sshd gone (qemu at ~115% CPU, port 2392 forwarding but every handshake closed)
attempts.root_cause: `ssh_vm 'sudo reboot'` returns immediately while sshd lingers, so the wait loop reconnected on its first 3s probe; the post-reboot phases therefore ran against the pre-reboot system and the delayed shutdown killed the transport mid-run. The same gate also reported phase-7 recovery PASS without any evidence that a reboot happened: in the previous attempt phase 7 began 5 seconds after phase 6, which cannot contain a reboot.
fix: record the guest boot id before the reboot, wait for the guest to become unreachable, wait for SSH to return, and require a changed boot id before the post-reboot phases run
the manifest host_reboot gate requires the same boot-id evidence, so a vacuous reboot can no longer be reported as PASS
qemu writes a serial console log which the trap copies into the evidence before teardown
attempts.consequence_for_earlier_evidence: any phase-7 'host reboot recovery' PASS recorded before this fix is not reboot evidence; the rc.23 reboot gate is only proven by a run with the fixed gate

attempts.outcome: FAILED at the reboot gate: the guest did not come back
attempts.classification: harness/environment defect (the gate itself behaved correctly)
observed: boot-id-before-reboot.txt recorded, boot-id-after-reboot.txt empty, campaign exit 1
guest-console.log ends in `libvirt-guests.sh: Waiting for 2 guests to shut down, 100 seconds left` and stops emitting
the retained guest was still unreachable minutes later, qemu at ~114% CPU
attempts.root_cause: the two nested tenant domains the campaign had running are CirrOS, which ignores the ACPI power button; stock Ubuntu libvirt-guests waits SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT=120s per batch and never forces a shutdown, so the host shutdown wedged waiting for guests that will never power off
attempts.not_a_product_defect_because: the same console log shows o3kd.service and o3k-compute.service stopping cleanly, so no O3K unit is implicated; the interaction is between the host distribution's libvirt-guests policy and a tenant image that does not implement ACPI shutdown
attempts.fix: bound the tenant shutdown before rebooting (ACPI shutdown for every running domain, short bounded wait, then virsh destroy for anything still running) and record both listings as evidence; raise the comeback window to 12 minutes
attempts.positive_evidence: the boot-id gate introduced in de634dec refused to report the reboot as proven, and the console capture introduced in the same commit produced the diagnosis

attempts.outcome: FAILED at phase 8: the exact public installer rerun aborted in its demo stage
attempts.classification: harness sizing interaction, not a product defect
observed: host reboot verified: guest boot id changed (the fixed gate now proves a real reboot)
phase 7 PASS: post-reboot identity, durable BuildingBlock and provider domain preserved

rerun-install.log: the installer verified and reinstalled the runtime, then 'compute host could not satisfy placement requirements (HTTP 409)' and 'TestLab bootstrap failed: server creation failed: test-vm'
attempts.root_cause: O3K reports the guest's own CPU count and disk as compute inventory. With the campaign host at -smp 2 the inventory was VCPU 2/2 once the campaign's pp4-native and pp4-openstack servers were running, so the installer's demo stage had no vCPU left for its own test-vm. The installer reported that truthfully and aborted; no O3K code was at fault.
attempts.note_on_phase_1_inventory: the DISK_GB 10 / MEMORY_MB 512 / VCPU 1 recorded at phase 1 is the installer's demo test-vm itself, captured before the campaign deleted it, not a leaked allocation
attempts.fix: size the campaign host for the required matrix: 4 vCPUs and a 48 GB overlay, so the rerun's demo workload fits alongside the campaign's servers. The rerun gate keeps its original strength instead of being weakened to accommodate an undersized host.
positive_evidence: the boot-id gate proved a genuine reboot (boot-id-before-reboot.txt differs from boot-id-after-reboot.txt)
the tenant domains were destroyed by the bounded shutdown and O3K reconciled them back to running after the reboot
the public installer verified the exact rc.23 artifact and reinstalled the runtime before the demo stage ran out of capacity

manifest_gate_defects.observed: generate_core_manifest.py reported canonical_replay and changed_body_conflict as NOT PROVEN for a run whose phase 3 asserted both, forcing verdict=BLOCKED and contradicting the phase log of the same run
manifest_gate_defects.root_cause: the manifest compared side-effects-before/after snapshots byte-for-byte, while the accepted invariant asserted in-run compares only resources, operations, network_ports, placement_allocations and the replaying operation's own quota reservation count
manifest_gate_defects.why_the_raw_counts_differ: a replayed request legitimately records one additional quota_reservations row (8 -> 9) while the per-operation reservation count stays 1 and no canonical resource, operation, port or Placement allocation is duplicated
manifest_gate_defects.verified_against: preserved evidence of attempt complete-1: canonical_replay PASS and changed_body_conflict PASS after the fix
manifest_gate_defects.residual_transparency: the manifest keeps the raw before/after counts, so replay_side_effects.quota_reservations.duplicate stays true while the gate verdict is PASS; the tolerated row-count delta is visible, not hidden
